scope: Theorem 10.1 (LQG metric inputs) of the manuscript “Canonical conformal limits of subcritical FK planar maps” (preprints/Canonical-conformal-limits-of-subcritical-FK-planar-maps-September-24-2026/main.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 211 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 e7dab39caf778176), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 84. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: The subcritical LQG metric is a field-measurable continuous length metric inducing the surface topology. Its internal metric on U is determined by h|U . It obeys Dh+f = eξf · Dh, µh+f = eγf µh, (10.1) Dh◦ψ+Q log |ψ′|(z, w) = Dh(ψ(z), ψ(w)) (10.2) for continuous f and conformal coordinate maps ψ. The whole-plane GFF metric is proper and geodesic, and the geodesic between each fixed pair of distinct points is almost surely unique. For every compact planar set and every 0 < β < ξ(Q − 2), there are almost surely finite C and positive r0 such that, for |z − w| < r0 in that set, Dh(z, w; B2|z−w|(z)) ≤ C|z − w|β . (10.3) The corresponding estimates before almost-sure truncation have polynomially high probability uniformly over the reference scale, with the normalization rξQeξhr(0).
